text:
alex: Quick report — mypy/pyright failing in the sample app when using autogen models + async client. Root message: generated models use very loose types (Dict[str, Any]) and streaming API stubs show AsyncIterator[Any]. Example error: `error: Incompatible return value type (got "AsyncIterator[Dict[str, Any]]", expected "AsyncIterator[ChatMessage]")`. Anyone seen this?

marta: Seen it. Codegen currently emits `Any` for unions and optional fields when it can't decide. Also we don't generate TypedDicts for plain response shapes which trips pyright.

sam: Related: the async `stream_chat` helper is typed as `AsyncIterator[Any]` because the generator emits raw dicts before model parsing. mypy wants a concrete type. Both mypy/pyright flag usages in our samples.

alex: Minimal repro snippet I used:

```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from typing import AsyncIterator

client = AsyncClient()

async def fetch() -> AsyncIterator[ChatMessage]:
    async for chunk in client.stream_chat("hello"):
        yield chunk  # mypy: error here, chunk: Dict[str, Any]
```

The generator signature in the stub is `async def stream_chat(...) -> AsyncIterator[Dict[str, Any]]` which forces the error.

marta: Quick workaround: cast the yielded value after parsing, e.g. `msg = ChatMessage.parse_obj(chunk); yield cast(ChatMessage, msg)` but that's noisy for users. Better to fix the generator typing.

sam: Agreed. Options: (1) change codegen to emit `AsyncIterator[ChatMessage]` and ensure runtime returns model instances, (2) produce .pyi stubs mapping runtime shape to types, or (3) add an opt-in mypy plugin/config in sample apps to ignore those calls. I prefer (1).

marta: Implementation note: generator pipeline currently does: raw stream -> yield raw chunk -> later sample wrapper does `ChatMessage.parse_obj`. We can flip order in the client: parse into ChatMessage before yielding. That keeps runtime unchanged except ordering and makes typing straightforward.

alex: That would be ideal. Any risk parsing before yield for large streaming payloads? Performance/latency tradeoffs?

marta: Parsing is pretty cheap per chunk; we should benchmark but it's likely fine. We'll add an option `parse_stream=True` in client config to preserve old behavior.

ci-bot: CI status: mypy job failed on `examples/chat/async_streaming.py` in PR #542 — 1 error.

devex-qa: Can we add a small typing test to catch regressions? e.g., mypy check under `examples/` in CI matrix. Also add a pyright check for the TS translation of samples.

sam: I'll draft a .pyi for the streaming API as fallback while marta works on generator change. Keeps sample apps green.

marta: I'll take the fix. Plan: change client to parse before yield, add `parse_stream` flag default True, add unit + mypy test for examples, update changelog. Will open PR later today. ETA: EOD PT.

alex: Thanks. Please add a short migration note in `docs/clients/python.md` and a snippet for users who rely on old behavior.

devex-qa: Also add a note in release notes about pyright/mypy fixes and mention the opt-out flag.

alex: Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/2789 (assigning to @marta).

marta: Got it, looking now. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll leave a draft .pyi in the PR as well.

ci-bot: PR created: #548 — `fix(python-client): typed streaming responses and mypy tests` (status: draft)

alex: Nice. Follow-up: we should scan other generated endpoints for similar loose typing (embeddings, rerank). Can we add a lint step in codegen to flag `Any` in public signatures?

marta: Good idea. I'll add a codegen rule to warn on `Any` in exported signatures.

sam: Cool. Thanks everyone.

alex: Closing loop — please ping this thread when PR moves out of draft.
